fact_text: PABC is described as Pakistan's only aluminium beverage can manufacturer.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst estimates that about 90% of beverage cans bought in Pakistan were made by PABC.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PABC's Faisalabad plant began operating in 2017 inside a special economic zone that gives the company a 10-year income tax exemption.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PABC's income tax exemption from the special economic zone is set to expire in 2028; without it, the analyst estimates local sales would face close to 40% tax including super tax.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Total investment in the 1.2 billion-can plant is about USD 100 million, including roughly USD 70-80 million for the 2017 plant and about USD 25 million across two later minor expansions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PABC's nameplate capacity is 1.2 billion cans a year, but about 1 billion cans a year is a realistic maximum given design changeovers, different can sizes and seasonality.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Most single-serve beverages in Pakistan are still sold in plastic bottles, and PABC's main local customers are the Pepsi and Coca-Cola bottlers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Afghanistan is PABC's main export market, where can demand is almost three times Pakistan's because aluminium cans have a high share of the single-serve market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PABC's plant is the closest can plant to Kabul, and the company invoices its cans in US dollars, mostly selling to multinational bottlers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Besides Afghanistan, PABC exports to Tajikistan, Sri Lanka and Uzbekistan, but the analyst regards those markets as earning much thinner profits.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Local can sales earn a higher profit per can than exports, so local volume is the main driver of PABC's profit, with export markets contributing less.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Dollar pricing shields PABC from rupee devaluation, but a local economic slowdown cuts can demand and hits local sales, which is the largest driver of profit variation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The main export risk is closure of the Chaman border, while payment risk is low because PABC mostly sells to multinational bottlers and sometimes takes advance payments.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PABC's sales are seasonal: cold winters in Afghanistan and northern Pakistan reduce can demand, which makes Q1 and Q4 the weak quarters.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Return on invested capital can be estimated as capacity times utilisation times profit per can, divided by capital invested; the analyst's example gives about 15% in dollar terms at 80% utilisation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because PABC earns in dollars, the analyst expects rupee-denominated returns to run above dollar returns, the gap reflecting expected rupee depreciation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When calculating future ROIC, keep a margin of safety by assuming a lower profit per unit and a utilisation rate below the plant's typical level, as the analyst did with 80% utilisation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst values PABC by using the owners' dividend payout policy as the benchmark, since minority shareholders realise value only through dividends or selling on the stock market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Each industry needs its own valuation approach: in cement, value realisation is linked to the cost of the plant per unit of capacity, while other sectors need grouping by shareholder behaviour.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst estimates a stock's value two to three years out from expected earnings and dividend payout, rather than from the near-term share price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treats an expected 30-35% annual return over about three years as the point at which a holding's value realisation is considered locked in.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's three-step framework is: understand the business like an owner, estimate value realisation over two to three years, then check whether the company ranks among the top seven to eight ideas.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Before concluding on a company, the analyst reads about five years of its reports, including annual and industry reports, to avoid missing links in understanding the business.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST IN WHAT YOU FULLY UNDERSTAND' (YouTube transcript, undated)
